name: Neurological channelopathy of the central nervous system due to a genetic potassium channel defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in potassium channel gene associated with CNS channelopathy
Presence of recurrent episodic neurological symptoms such as ataxia, seizures, or paralysis
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses through clinical, imaging, and laboratory evaluation
Electrophysiological studies showing abnormal neuronal excitability consistent with potassium channel dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic potassium channel gene mutation plus presence of recurrent episodic neurological symptoms and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary depending on specific gene involved.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizure episodes with focal or generalized onset

searchTerms: weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs
mild problems with automatic body functions

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations including anxiety or mood disorders
Respiratory muscle weakness leading to dyspnea
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Possible elevated creatine kinase during episodes
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebellar atrophy or be normal
No specific structural abnormalities in most cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in potassium channel genes such as KCNA1, KCNQ2, or KCNMA1
other: Electromyography (EMG) may show abnormal muscle excitability

distinguishingFeatures: CACNA1A gene mutation instead of potassium channel gene
More prominent cerebellar signs and migraine
Presence of migraine with aura and hemiplegia
Mutations in CACNA1A, ATP1A2, or SCN1A genes
Autoimmune etiology with acetylcholine receptor antibodies
Fluctuating muscle weakness without episodic paralysis

redFlags: Sudden onset of paralysis with respiratory compromise
Refractory seizures despite standard antiepileptic therapy
references: Orphanet: Neurological channelopathies due to potassium channel defects, ORPHA:98746
Imbrici P, et al. Potassium channelopathies of the central nervous system. Front Cell Neurosci. 2013.
Kullmann DM. Neurological channelopathies. Annu Rev Neurosci. 2010.
